title: Modal perfect
use_hint: Fix the sentence · Enter = check · Enter = next
note: B2 grammar unit, drafted 2026-09-05 on the home lane, replacing the empty stub. 30 items, inside the 24-40 band. The two predecessors divide cleanly and neither is re-taught: b1_modals_speculation (48) owns PRESENT speculation (might/may/could/must + be) and b1_past_modals (25) owns past ability and obligation (had to / was able to / managed to). What neither has is modal + **have** + past participle, which is this unit. Two blocks: how sure about the past (14 — must have / cannot have / might have) and looking back with should (10 — should have / should not have). The teaching spine is the one Czech learners actually get wrong: THE NEGATIVE OF `must have` IS `cannot have`, never *must not have*. That is stated on the certainty card, sits in the distractors (B4), and is Use item 2. C43: the certainty card names its axis rather than just listing forms. C57: card 1 recaps the Modals 8 scale and moves it into the past. A0/A5: the possibility items carry gap_accepts [might, may, could] so all three grade correct, since the Czech *možná* does not pick one; the chips offer only one of the three so the Quiz stays single-answer. A8 accepts are a full contraction closure (cannot/can't, should not/shouldn't). D1: every item has its own explanation naming its own verb and its own evidence. gap_class auxiliary on all 24 gap items, per FCE-EXERCISES. KWT-native per that spec, but KWT needs a js/ branch that is James-only under P-engine, so Use is ordinary error-correction (E7), one real error each (E2).

cards.title: Modal perfect
points: A modal plus **have** plus a past participle looks back at the past.
The modal says how sure you are, or what should have happened.
The **have** never disappears: *must have left*, not *must left*.

cards.title: You already know
points: Modals 8 put the guessing scale in the **present**.

cards.title: How sure, about the past
points: The axis is **how sure** you are that something happened.
Evidence decides which one you use.
The opposite of *must have* is **cannot have** — not *must not have*.

rows: Her coat is gone. She **must have** left.
He was in Prague. She **cannot have** seen him.

cards.title: Looking back with should
points: **should have** = the right thing, which did not happen.
**should not** have = it did happen, and it was wrong.
This is criticism or regret, not a guess.

cards.title: Common mistakes
points: Every one of these drops the *have*, or gets the participle wrong.

items.en: She must have left already — her coat is gone.
items.cz: Musela už odejít — kabát je pryč.
items.gap: She ____ have left already — her coat is gone.
accepts: She must have left already — her coat is gone.
items.explanation: The coat is the evidence, so this is a certainty about the past: **must** have left.
items.explanation_cz: Kabát je důkaz, takže je to jistota o minulosti: **must** have left.

items.en: He must have known about it, because he was there.
items.cz: Musel o tom vědět, protože tam byl.
items.gap: He ____ have known about it, because he was there.
accepts: He must have known about it, because he was there.
items.explanation: *He was there* forces the deduction — **must** have known.
items.explanation_cz: *He was there* vynucuje ten závěr — **must** have known.

items.en: They must have finished the work by now.
items.gap: They ____ have finished the work by now.
accepts: They must have finished the work by now.
items.explanation: **must** have finished — you are sure, based on how much time has passed.
items.explanation_cz: **must** have finished — jsi si jistý podle toho, kolik času uběhlo.

items.en: You must have been very tired after that journey.
items.cz: Po té cestě jsi musel být hrozně unavený.
items.gap: You ____ have been very tired after that journey.
accepts: You must have been very tired after that journey.
items.explanation: **must** have been — a confident guess about how someone felt.
items.explanation_cz: **must** have been — jistý odhad, jak se někdo cítil.

items.en: Somebody must have taken my umbrella.
items.gap: Somebody ____ have taken my umbrella.
accepts: Somebody must have taken my umbrella.
items.explanation: The umbrella is gone, so **must** have taken is the only reading.
items.explanation_cz: Deštník je pryč, takže **must** have taken je jediné čtení.

items.en: She cannot have seen the film — it was not in cinemas yet.
items.cz: Ten film nemohla vidět — ještě nebyl v kinech.
items.gap: She ____ have seen the film — it was not in cinemas yet.
accepts: She can't have seen the film — it wasn't in cinemas yet.
She can't have seen the film — it was not in cinemas yet.
She cannot have seen the film — it wasn't in cinemas yet.
She can not have seen the film — it wasn't in cinemas yet.
She cannot have seen the film — it was not in cinemas yet.
She can not have seen the film — it was not in cinemas yet.
items.explanation: The film was not out yet, so it is ruled out. The negative of *must have* is **cannot have** — never *must not have*.
items.explanation_cz: Film ještě nebyl venku, takže je to vyloučené. Zápor od *must have* je **cannot have** — nikdy *must not have*.

items.en: He cannot have written that letter himself.
items.gap: He ____ have written that letter himself.
accepts: He can't have written that letter himself.
He cannot have written that letter himself.
He can not have written that letter himself.
items.explanation: **cannot** have written — you are sure it did not happen.
items.explanation_cz: **cannot** have written — jsi si jistý, že se to nestalo.

items.en: They cannot have arrived yet, the train is late.
items.cz: Ještě nemohli dorazit, vlak má zpoždění.
items.gap: They ____ have arrived yet, the train is late.
accepts: They can't have arrived yet, the train is late.
They cannot have arrived yet, the train is late.
They can not have arrived yet, the train is late.
items.explanation: The late train makes it impossible — **cannot** have arrived.
items.explanation_cz: Zpožděný vlak to znemožňuje — **cannot** have arrived.

items.en: You cannot have finished already — it is only ten.
items.cz: Nemůžeš být hotový — je teprve deset.
items.gap: You ____ have finished already — it is only ten.
accepts: You can't have finished already — it's only ten.
You can't have finished already — it is only ten.
You cannot have finished already — it's only ten.
You can not have finished already — it's only ten.
You cannot have finished already — it is only ten.
You can not have finished already — it is only ten.
items.explanation: **cannot** have finished. The time is the evidence against it.
items.explanation_cz: **cannot** have finished. Ten čas je důkaz proti.

items.en: They might have missed the train.
items.gap: They ____ have missed the train.
accepts: They might have missed the train.
items.explanation: You do not know — **might** have missed. *May* and *could* work the same way.
items.explanation_cz: Nevíš to — **might** have missed. *May* a *could* fungují stejně.

items.en: She might have forgotten about the meeting.
items.gap: She ____ have forgotten about the meeting.
accepts: She might have forgotten about the meeting.
items.explanation: **might** have forgotten — one possible explanation, not a certainty.
items.explanation_cz: **might** have forgotten — jedno možné vysvětlení, ne jistota.

items.en: He might have left his phone at home.
items.gap: He ____ have left his phone at home.
accepts: He might have left his phone at home.
items.explanation: **might** have left — a guess with no evidence either way.
items.explanation_cz: **might** have left — odhad bez důkazu na obě strany.

items.en: We might have met before, but I am not sure.
items.cz: Možná jsme se už potkali, ale nejsem si jistý.
items.gap: We ____ have met before, but I am not sure.
accepts: We might have met before, but I'm not sure.
We might have met before, but I am not sure.
items.explanation: *I am not sure* names the uncertainty — **might** have met.
items.explanation_cz: *I am not sure* pojmenovává nejistotu — **might** have met.

items.en: Somebody might have moved the papers.
items.gap: Somebody ____ have moved the papers.
accepts: Somebody might have moved the papers.
items.explanation: **might** have moved — nobody knows who, or whether.
items.explanation_cz: **might** have moved — nikdo neví kdo ani jestli.

items.en: You should have told me about the change.
items.cz: Měl jsi mi o té změně říct.
items.gap: You ____ have told me about the change.
accepts: You should have told me about the change.
items.explanation: **should** have told — looking back at the right thing that was not done.
items.explanation_cz: **should** have told — ohlédnutí za správnou věcí, která se neudělala.

items.en: I should have asked before I bought it.
items.cz: Měl jsem se zeptat, než jsem to koupil.
items.gap: I ____ have asked before I bought it.
accepts: I should have asked before I bought it.
items.explanation: **should** have asked — regret about your own past choice.
items.explanation_cz: **should** have asked — lítost nad vlastní minulou volbou.

items.en: She should have listened to her doctor.
items.gap: She ____ have listened to her doctor.
accepts: She should have listened to her doctor.
items.explanation: **should** have listened — criticism of a past decision.
items.explanation_cz: **should** have listened — kritika minulého rozhodnutí.

items.en: We should have booked the table earlier.
items.cz: Měli jsme si ten stůl rezervovat dřív.
items.gap: We ____ have booked the table earlier.
accepts: We should have booked the table earlier.
items.explanation: **should** have booked — the booking did not happen, and it was a mistake.
items.explanation_cz: **should** have booked — rezervace se nestala a byla to chyba.

items.en: They should have checked the address first.
items.cz: Měli si nejdřív ověřit tu adresu.
items.gap: They ____ have checked the address first.
accepts: They should have checked the address first.
items.explanation: **should** have checked — the right action, taken too late or not at all.
items.explanation_cz: **should** have checked — správný krok, provedený pozdě nebo vůbec.

items.en: You should not have said that to her.
items.gap: You ____ have said that to her.
accepts: You shouldn't have said that to her.
You should not have said that to her.
items.explanation: **should not** have said — it DID happen, and it was wrong. *Shouldn't* is the same answer.
items.explanation_cz: **should not** have said — stalo se to a bylo to špatně. *Shouldn't* je totéž.

items.en: He should not have driven after the party.
items.gap: He ____ have driven after the party.
accepts: He shouldn't have driven after the party.
He should not have driven after the party.
items.explanation: **should not** have driven — criticism of something he actually did.
items.explanation_cz: **should not** have driven — kritika něčeho, co opravdu udělal.

items.en: I should not have eaten so much.
items.gap: I ____ have eaten so much.
accepts: I shouldn't have eaten so much.
I should not have eaten so much.
items.explanation: **should not** have eaten — regret about a past action of your own.
items.explanation_cz: **should not** have eaten — lítost nad vlastním minulým činem.

items.en: She should not have left the door open.
items.gap: She ____ have left the door open.
accepts: She shouldn't have left the door open.
She should not have left the door open.
items.explanation: **should not** have left — the door was left open, and that was the mistake.
items.explanation_cz: **should not** have left — dveře zůstaly otevřené a to byla chyba.

items.en: We should not have waited so long.
items.gap: We ____ have waited so long.
accepts: We shouldn't have waited so long.
We should not have waited so long.
items.explanation: **should not** have waited — the waiting happened and it cost you.
items.explanation_cz: **should not** have waited — čekání proběhlo a stálo tě to.

items.en: She must have left already.
accepts: She must have left already.
items.explanation: A modal needs **have** before the past participle: *must have left*.
items.explanation_cz: Modální sloveso potřebuje před příčestím **have**: *must have left*.

items.en: He cannot have known about it.
items.wrong: He must not have known about it.
accepts: He can't have known about it.
He cannot have known about it.
He can not have known about it.
items.explanation: The opposite of *must have* is **cannot have**. *Must not have* is not English here.
items.explanation_cz: Opak *must have* je **cannot have**. *Must not have* tu není angličtina.

items.en: You should have told me about the change.
items.cz: Měl jsi mi o té změně říct.
items.wrong: You should told me about the change.
accepts: You should have told me about the change.
items.explanation: **should have** + past participle. The *have* cannot be dropped.
items.explanation_cz: **should have** + příčestí minulé. *Have* se vynechat nedá.

items.en: I should have gone earlier.
accepts: I should have gone earlier.
items.explanation: After *have* comes the past participle: **gone**, not *went*.
items.explanation_cz: Po *have* následuje příčestí minulé: **gone**, ne *went*.

items.en: They might have missed the train.
accepts: They might have missed the train.
items.explanation: **might have** + past participle — the *have* carries the past.
items.explanation_cz: **might have** + příčestí minulé — *have* nese minulost.

items.en: She cannot have seen the film yesterday.
items.wrong: She cannot have saw the film yesterday.
accepts: She can't have seen the film yesterday.
She cannot have seen the film yesterday.
She can not have seen the film yesterday.
items.explanation: After *have* the form is the past participle: **seen**, not *saw*.
items.explanation_cz: Po *have* je tvar příčestí minulé: **seen**, ne *saw*.
